answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings: every square depends on the preceding result, so GPUs cannot compress one identity’s elapsed time through parallel execution. Cloning identities creates independent chains, each demanding its own sustained sequential budget; hardware may multiply, but delay per clone remains. A grove of clones cannot become an oasis of instant identities because the verified output is an anchor for admission.
